source:
Create a polished 3D Roblox RNG game called "Cosmic RNG".

Core Gameplay

- Players spawn in a colorful 3D lobby.
- Add a large ROLL button on the screen.
- When the player rolls, generate a random rarity.
- Rarities should include:
 - Common - 1/2
 - Uncommon - 1/5
 - Rare - 1/25
 - Epic - 1/100
 - Legendary - 1/500
 - Mythic - 1/2,500
 - Cosmic - 1/10,000
- Show the obtained rarity with a satisfying animation, sound effect, particles, and floating text.
- Give each rarity a unique 3D aura/effect around the player's character.
- Players can open an Inventory to view everything they have collected.
- Add a Luck stat that can increase through gameplay.
- Add a leaderboard showing the players with the rarest rolls.
- Include a pity system so players eventually receive a higher rarity after many unlucky rolls.
- Add a shop where players can buy cosmetic effects and temporary luck boosts using in-game currency.

3D World

Create a futuristic floating-island map with:

- A central spawn area
- Roll platform
- Inventory/shop buildings
- Floating crystals
- Glowing portals
- Decorative clouds and particles
- A large skybox with planets and stars

UI

Make the UI clean and mobile-friendly:

- Large Roll button
- Current luck
- Roll counter
- Inventory button
- Shop button
- Leaderboard button
- Recent roll notification

Important

Make the game fully playable, not just a visual mockup. Add the necessary Roblox scripts, UI interactions, random rarity system, inventory system, saving/loading of player data, leaderboards, and effects. Make sure everything works on both mobile and PC.

image_prompt.text: The central spawn area of the floating island, open and sized for a crowd of players to stand around in
The roll platform as a large distinct structure at the heart of the island, visible from anywhere on it
Where players arrive on the island, placed so the first thing they see is the roll platform
Glowing portals set around the island
A futuristic floating island suspended in space, with the map's edges dropping away into sky
Separate inventory and shop buildings with sleek futuristic architecture
Large floating crystals drifting above and around the island
Decorative clouds and drifting particles around the island edges

layout_placement.text: Player arrival point on the central island
Paired portal markers, if the portals are meant to move players rather than just glow
A trigger on the roll platform where the roll is performed

notes: No genre matched. An RNG roller is a real game type with no entry in the index - see gaps.genre_gap - so it was built as a decorated lobby through no-genre.
All five axes are at default, so the route is P0. If players go inside the inventory and shop buildings rather than walking up to them, that becomes P3 - worth confirming before generation.
The prompt's portals are listed among decorations, so it is not clear they lead anywhere. teleporter-link is carried on the assumption they do; drop it if they are set dressing.
Almost everything else in this prompt - rarities, luck, pity, inventory, leaderboard, saving - is UI and progression with no spatial footprint.

open_questions.ask: Is this one island you can cross in a few seconds, or a spread of islands with distance between them?
Do players walk inside the inventory and shop buildings, or interact from outside?
Do the glowing portals actually take players somewhere, or are they decoration?

theme: Colourful futuristic cosmic - sleek glowing surfaces, planets and stars overhead

coverage_missing.ask: Is standing in the lobby and pressing Roll the whole game, or is there anywhere to go?
Are the shop and inventory buildings enterable?
How big should the island be - a plaza, or something you walk across?

answers.ask: Is this one island you can cross in a few seconds, or a spread of islands with distance between them?
answers.answer: Use one compact central floating island that players can cross in a few seconds, with smaller nearby decorative islands in the background.

answers.ask: Do players walk inside the inventory and shop buildings, or interact from outside?
answers.answer: Players interact with the inventory and shop from outside via clearly marked building entrances or prompts; no interior spaces are needed.

answers.ask: Do the glowing portals actually take players somewhere, or are they decoration?
answers.answer: The glowing portals are decorative for this first build and do not take players anywhere.
